title: Flickering Lights: How to Diagnose and Fix It
metaDescription: Lights flickering in one room or the whole house? Here's how to tell if it's a cheap bulb/dimmer fix or a wiring issue that needs an electrician.
symptom: One or more light fixtures flicker, dim briefly, or flash — either occasionally or every time a large appliance kicks on.
partsNeeded: Compatible dimmer switch (only if an incompatible dimmer is the cause)

steps.heading: Rule out the bulb first
steps.body: A loose or failing bulb is the single most common cause of flickering in a single fixture. Turn off power to the fixture, then tighten the bulb (LEDs and CFLs can flicker if not seated fully) or swap in a bulb you know is good.

steps.heading: Check if it's on a dimmer
steps.body: Many LED bulbs flicker on older dimmer switches that weren't designed for LED loads. If the fixture is dimmable, try the bulb in a non-dimmed fixture — if the flicker stops, you need an LED-compatible dimmer, not a new bulb.

steps.heading: Notice the pattern: one fixture vs. whole room vs. whole house
steps.body: Flickering isolated to one fixture usually means the bulb, socket, or switch. Flickering that happens house-wide, especially in sync with a large appliance (AC, dryer, well pump) turning on, points to a bigger issue — a loose main connection or an overloaded shared circuit.

steps.heading: Check for a loose connection at the switch (with power off)
steps.body: If it's isolated to one switch/fixture, turn off the breaker for that circuit, confirm it's dead with a voltage tester, then check that the wire connections at the switch are snug — a loose neutral or hot connection is a common flicker cause.

steps.heading: Watch for whole-house flickering, which is not a DIY fix
steps.body: If lights flicker throughout the entire house, especially when large appliances cycle on, this often points to a loose connection at the meter or panel — a serious issue that can damage appliances and is a fire risk. Don't attempt to trace this past the switch level yourself.

whenToCallAPro: If flickering happens across multiple rooms or the whole house, syncs with large appliances turning on, or continues after ruling out the bulb and dimmer, call a licensed electrician — a loose connection at the panel or meter is a genuine fire hazard and isn't something to keep monitoring.
safetyWarnings: Always switch off the breaker and confirm it's dead with a voltage tester before opening any switch or fixture — don't rely on the wall switch alone.
Whole-house flickering, especially with a burning smell or warm outlets/switch plates, means stop investigating yourself and call an electrician immediately.
